default_exit._why: one exit for every family so rules compete on the same footing; the owner will decide the demo stop/take-profit later and this block changes then (a change = a new screen run, its variants counted again)
default_exit._fills: signal at the close of bar t; market order at the open of the 1-minute bar that starts at t's close (+ slippage); every 1-minute bar from the entry minute on: stop first (fills at the stop or the gap open, - slippage), then the target (a limit: needs a trade 1 tick through, fills at the target); time exit at the open of the first minute at or after entry + max_hold_min; flat at the session's flatten time; one position at a time; at most max_entries_per_session entries per session

E-559.title: Same-minute return sign persistence
E-559.hypothesis: Recurring clients (hedges, index rebalancers, ADR arbitrage) trade the same time window every day; if the trailing move into this minute had the same sign in most of the last 20 sessions, follow that sign.

E-560.title: Rolling-window VWAP stretch fade
E-560.hypothesis: Liquidity takers who push price far from the last hour's volume-weighted fair value pay to do so; the dealers who absorb it revert price toward the rolling VWAP.

E-561.title: Bar-gap pressure follow
E-561.hypothesis: A bar that opens above the previous close means the book was swept by aggressive market buys between prints; a run of such gap-ups shows one-sided urgency that continues.

E-562.title: Afternoon-anchored VWAP stretch fade
E-562.hypothesis: Afternoon participants start from a fresh cost basis; a stretch from the VWAP anchored at midday, measured against its own typical stretch, is a late chase that reverts.

E-563.title: Chaikin money-flow thrust follow
E-563.hypothesis: When bars close near their highs (or lows) on volume repeatedly, the volume-weighted close location shows persistent buying (selling) pressure that carries on.

E-564.title: Return-volume correlation follow
E-564.hypothesis: When volume rises with up-moves (and falls with pullbacks) the move is driven by informed demand and continues; positive return-volume correlation plus a net move gives the side.

E-565.title: Day-open recross follow
E-565.hypothesis: The day's open is the price where the overnight imbalance resolved; after a long stay on one side, the first close through it shows the other side has taken control.

E-566.title: Trend-significance follow
E-566.hypothesis: A statistically significant slope of price over the window (t-stat of the regression) separates a real directional flow from noise; follow when the t-statistic first crosses the threshold.

E-567.title: Median-anchored range stretch fade
E-567.hypothesis: The rolling median ignores the burst prints that drag a mean; a close several average bar-ranges away from the median is an overshoot by impatient flow and reverts.
